newsitem.title: CHINA: Shanghai B share index ends at record low.
newsitem.headline: Shanghai B share index ends at record low.

text.p: Shanghai's B share index ended down 0.483 points or 1.02 percent at a record low of 46.652 points on Wednesday due to overseas liquidation, brokers said.
This is the second time in a week that the index hit an all-time low, since the Shanghai bourse was set up in 1990. The previous low was 46.731 points set on Thursday last week.

"Overseas liquidation continued today, with domestic institutions failing to support the market," said one trader. "With the market in a deep depression over the past two years, even the institutions seem to have lost confidence."

"Investors believe there will be no market-boosting measures from the central government in the short term," said a second trader. "Domestic investors are staying out of the market, so that thin overseas liquidation easily brought down the index."
The market has been on a downward trend in the past few weeks due to a lack of government support, with Beijing repeatedly re-affirming a ban on domestic trading of B shares, brokers said.
In addition, many key Shanghai B share companies have reported sharp falls in profits over the past two years, disheartening foreign investors, they said.
"There is no sign that the market will recover in the short term," said a Shanghai-based investment analyst with a foreign brokerage.
Shanghai Jinjiang Tower was the day's biggest loser on speculative selling, falling $0.012 or 5.22 percent to $0.218, on volume of only 30 shares.
Huaxin Cement was the second biggest loser, shedding $0.010 or 5.00 percent to $0.190, on volume of 30,000 shares.
Shanghai Lujiazui Finance and Trade Zone Development traded the most, on volume of 1.7 million shares. It lost $0.002 to $0.878.
Combined B share trading volume was thin at 6.4 million shares worth $2.5 million.

Shanghai's A share index closed down 13.728 points or 1.41 percent to 962.449 points due to continued rumours that the securities authorities would crack down on the market by investigating illegal credit trading by brokerages, brokers said.
Combined A share volume was 330.5 million worth 2.9 billion yuan. The SSE 30 blue-chip index fell 42.656 points or 1.74 percent to 2,409.203 points.
Chengdu Gongyi Metallurgy was the biggest loser on heavy profit-taking after surges in the past few days, down 0.66 yuan or 8.06 percent to 7.53 yuan, on volume of 3.9 million shares.
